text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"Boston","level":"city","category":"screening_restrictions","status":"in_force","title":"Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND)","requirement":"Housing providers that receive DND funding and/or land, or that have income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, may not impose a blanket denial of housing based on arrests or convictions and must assess applicants case by case. When determining eligibility or considering eviction, they may not consider: arrests that did not result in conviction (including dismissed charges and diversion programs); convictions subject to judicial relief (expungement, sealing, certificates of relief from disabilities); juvenile records; or convictions more than 5 years old. These limits do not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought, or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others, and they do not apply to current criminal behavior. Where those exceptions are considered, factors include rehabilitation, time elapsed since the conviction, and age at the time of conviction. On credit, the agent agrees not to use an applicant's credit score to approve or deny applications. Credit history may be used only in lieu of rental history, when rental history is unavailable, to judge ability to pay. A lack of credit history, as opposed to poor credit history, is not sufficient justification to reject an applicant. Ability to pay must be shown by an identifiable source of sufficient income and prior rental history.
